value.means: The stores Contoso trades from as this bundle records them: 57 rows, one per premises that is still open (no close date) and stands on a real site (the online outlet excluded). Each row is one shop, with the site it stands on, its name, the country and the state/region it sits in, when it opened, and its floor area — no country filter yet, no period, no sales. The 16 shut or restructured premises and the single web shop are not in here.

turns.did:
SELECT
  s.country_code AS store_country,
  l.country_code AS site_country,
  COUNT(*) AS stores,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.state) AS distinct_store_states,
  COUNT(DISTINCT l.state) AS distinct_site_states
FROM contoso_served.dim_store AS s
JOIN contoso_served.dim_location AS l
  ON s.location_code = l.location_code
WHERE
  s.location_code <> -1
  AND s.close_date IS NULL
  AND (
    s.country_code = 'FR' OR l.country_code = 'FR'
  )
GROUP BY
  1,
  2
ORDER BY
  3 DESC

value.sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS how_many_store
FROM contoso_served.dim_store
WHERE
  location_code <> -1 AND close_date IS NULL AND country_code = 'FR'
value.means: One figure: Contoso has 7 shops in France. That is 7 physical premises whose own address is French, counted off the store register with no period and no reference to sales — not 7 sales outlets' worth of revenue, and not 7 sites with some re-tenanted. All 7 are open: France has no closed or restructured premises at all, so this is simultaneously the count of French shops trading and the count of French store rows the dimension holds.

readings.could_also_mean: every French premises ever on record including closed and restructured ones — ALSO 7, measured: France carries no closed row at all, so the open/closed fork moves nothing here even though it moves the global figure from 57 to 73
readings.declaration: store.resolution.active_is_the_absent_close_date (default: active) — applied, and now shown to be costless for France

readings.could_also_mean: a count of sites (location_code) — ALSO 7, since each French shop stands on its own site with no succession of tenancies
readings.declaration: dim_store.store_key#finer_than: location_code — the distinction exists, and here the two levels coincide

turns.why: Count the French stores, and in the same query price the one default I applied against the document's own reading — trading shops only (declared) versus every French premises on record (what `understood_as` assumed) — so the override is disclosed with a figure beside it.
turns.did:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE
    close_date IS NULL) AS stores_trading,
  COUNT(*) AS store_rows_all,
  COUNT(DISTINCT location_code) AS sites_all,
  COUNT(DISTINCT location_code) FILTER(WHERE
    close_date IS NULL) AS sites_trading,
  COUNT(DISTINCT state) FILTER(WHERE
    close_date IS NULL) AS regions_trading
FROM contoso_served.dim_store
WHERE
  location_code <> -1 AND country_code = 'FR'

blocked.needs: a city or town column on the store or on its site. `dim_store` serves only store_key, location_code, store_name, country_code, state, open_date, close_date, status_annotation, square_metres; `dim_location` serves only location_code, country_code, country_name, state, units_ever_here. Neither holds a city, and `dim_location.location_code` is an INTEGER site code that would answer '12, 13, 14' if bound to 'which cities'. The only city in the bundle is `dim_customer.city` (34,581 values, 453 French) which is (a) where a CUSTOMER lives, not where a shop stands, and (b) declared suppressed under DQ-IDENTIFYING-DIM_CUSTOMER-CITY and must not appear in an answer.
